title: White House national cyber director being replaced as nation reels from tech outages | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Sean Cairncross is being replaced as the White House national cyber director, administration officials confirmed on social media Thursday — a move that comes as the nation is still reeling from astring of cyber outages.

The exact circumstances of Cairncross’ departure were not immediately clear, but a source close to the White House said President Donald Trump “fully supported firing Sean Cairncross from his position as he lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job.”

The White House had previouslytoutedCairncross’ “extensive leadership experience” when he was confirmed to the role in 2025.

Cairncross was nominated by Trump and served as the Senate-confirmed national cyber director for more than a year. He also played a key role in the administration’s dealings with major AI firms.

Kirsten Davies, the Senate-confirmed chief information officer at the Defense Department, will take over the role in an acting capacity, the source said. Secretary of DefensePete Hegsethand Secretary of StateMarco Rubiocongratulated Davies in social media posts Thursday, with Hegseth writing that she has “proven herself to be a dedicated patriot and professional.”

In a social media post thanking Trump, Hegseth and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller on Thursday, Davies wrote that the country “stands in the crossroad of analog, digital, and quantum technologies, our American way of living increasingly interconnected.”

“Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come …but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future,” Davieswrote. “Under President Trump’s leadership we will have a more secure, resilient; and supercharged technological future.”

Cairncross said in a statement to CNN Thursday night, “It has been the honor of a lifetime to serve President Donald J. Trump. I leave my role as Director of Cyber incredibly proud of our work to strengthen America’s cybersecurity, protect our critical infrastructure, confront foreign threats, and position America to lead the world in Super Intelligence.”

He added, “None of it would have been possible without President Trump’s extraordinary leadership. He is a prolific leader who thinks bigger, moves faster, and inspires those around him to deliver. I will always be grateful for the opportunity to serve him and our great country.”

A White House official also confirmed to CNN that Cairncross is leaving the Trump administration entirely.

The Office of the National Cyber Director coordinates cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government.

Cairncross is the latest cyber official to leave the administration; last year, the Trump administrationfiredthe director and deputy director of the National Security Agency, the United States’ powerful cyber intelligence bureau.

Axiosfirst reported Cairncross’ departure.

The departure comes as the US deals with a string of major outages and tech failures that have created some fears among Americans and raised questions about how well the US protects itself online. Democrats have faulted the administration’s response to the outages and warned that the country’s cyber defenses aren’t keeping up with AI-driven threats.

While Trump has downplayed the situation, telling Americans to “relax,” Rubio took a different tack. Earlier this week in Manila, he addressed the disruptions, saying there was “zero evidence” that hackers, criminals or foreign governments were behind the tech outages, or that the incidents are connected.

Talking to reporters, Rubio also appeared to make a tacit acknowledgment that the administration had been less than open about the outages until now.

“The best way to deal with people’s uncertainty and discomfort is to share with them transparently what we know and what we believe and that’s why I came before you today,” Rubio said. “We are not under systemic attack.”

It was an attempt to soothe nerves after days of confusing and sometimes conflicting statements from other administration officials that had drawn harsh criticism, even from some staunch Trump allies.

The White House did not say when Cairncross’ last day will be.

The Senate will have to confirm whoever fills the role permanently.

CNN’s Kevin Liptak contributed to this report.

This story has been updated with additional details.
